learning_outcomes.title: Responds to announcements, instructions, and asks questions in English
Listens attentively to stories, poems, and answers questions accurately
Speaks about personal experiences, family, friends, school, and nature
Uses polite expressions and appropriate social courtesies in dialogue
Participates actively in role plays, dialogues, and language activities
Reads aloud poems and prose passages with proper pronunciation, pause, and intonation
Reads silently with comprehension and extracts main themes and supporting details
Infers meanings of unfamiliar words and phrases from contextual clues
Refers to dictionaries and word lists for definitions, spellings, and usage
Identifies and applies synonyms, antonyms, rhyming words, and collocations
Forms words using prefixes, suffixes, and morphological roots
Identifies and correctly utilizes parts of speech, articles, and prepositions
Applies correct punctuation marks, capitalization, and sentence mechanics
Constructs grammatically sound sentences utilizing appropriate verb tenses
Composes coherent short paragraphs, personal letters, notices, and messages
Develops guided stories from outlines and derives meaningful morals
Expresses critical thoughts, personal emotions, and aesthetic appreciation of literary texts
Quotes memorized stanzas of prescribed classical and contemporary poems accurately
Enriches active vocabulary through contextual antonyms, prefixes, and word games
Demonstrates creative writing skills and structured story-building capability

questions.question: Write a short note on Rainbow.
questions.answer: Rainbow: The rainbow is a beautiful natural wonder that appears in the sky after a rain shower. It is made up of seven colours: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange and Red. Each colour is beautiful and unique. When we see a rainbow, it makes us happy and fills our heart with joy.

questions.question: Compare a real bridge and a rainbow. Write one similarity and one difference between them.
questions.answer: Rivers: Rivers are flowing bodies of water that move across the land. They are the source of water for animals, plants and people. Rivers helps us in many ways, like providing water for drinking, irrigation and fishing. Rivers are also home to many aquatic animals like fish and crocodiles. People enjoy boating, swimming and playing near river side. Rivers are very important for our planet and our daily lives.

sections.title: VII. Story Development
sections.instructions:
Develop a story using the clues given below. (Difficult) (LO-43) (4 Marks)
Clues: Three friends .........two geese, a tortoise........lived ......a pond.......due to drought....pond dried......decide to migrate.........food, water.......geese fly.......tortoise can’t......devise a plan.......carry tortoise.....hold stick with their beaks....tortoise not to speak.....hold the middle of the stick......children clap....tortoise angry.....bursts out....fell.

questions.question: Develop a story of two geese and a tortoise using the given clues and write the moral.
questions.answer:
Two geese and a tortoise were friends. The geese wanted to migrate to a new place and asked the tortoise to join them. They devised a plan for the tortoise to hold onto a stick while the geese flew, carrying the stick. However, the tortoise was told not to speak. On the way, the tortoise couldn't resist responding to children's taunts, opened his mouth, and fell to his death. The story teaches the importance of self-control and following advice.
Moral: Self-control and listening to good advice saves life / Look before you leap.

sections.title: VIII. Dialogue Completion
sections.instructions: Complete the following conversation. (Difficult) (LO-14) (4 Marks)

questions.question:
Patient: Good morning, doctor.
Doctor: ______________________________
Patient: ______________________________
Doctor: Let me check your temperature. Yes, you have slight fever. When did the cough start?
Patient: ______________________________
Doctor: ______________________________
Patient: Should I go to school today?
Doctor: ______________________________
Patient: ______________________________
Doctor: You are welcome. Get well soon!
questions.answer:
Patient: Good morning, doctor.
Doctor: Very good morning. What seems to be the problem?
Patient: I have fever and bad cough.
Doctor: Let me check your temperature. Yes, you have slight fever. When did the cough start?
Patient: It started yesterday night. My throat also hurts.
Doctor: Don’t worry, it is just a common cold. I will give you some medicine. Take one tablet in the morning and one at night.
Patient: Should I go to school today?
Doctor: No, you need to rest at home for two days. Drink plenty of warm water.
Patient: Okay, Doctor. Thank you very much!
Doctor: You are welcome. Get well soon!

sections.title: VIII. Story Development

Develop a story using the clues given below. (Difficult) (LO-43) (2 Marks)
Clues: A hungry dog________ searching food _______fond of a bone_______ happy______ crossing a bridge _______saw own reflection _______another dog_____ bark_______ bone fell ____ water____ dog______ foolish_____ home_____ disappointed_____.

questions.question: Develop the story of the greedy dog using the clues and state the moral.
questions.answer:
Once upon a time, there was a hungry dog who loved to eat bones. One day, he found the juicy bone and held it in his mouth and was so happy that he had food. While crossing along a bridge, he looked down at the water and saw his own reflection with a bone holding in his mouth. He got so greedy that he wanted the other dog’s bone too. He barked at the other dog to try to get the bone, but when the mouth opened his own bone fell into the water. He lost his bone because he was too greedy.
Moral: BE HAPPY WITH WHAT YOU HAVE AND DON’T BE GREEDY.

sections.title: X. Detailed Analysis
sections.instructions: Answer the following question in about 8-10 sentences. (Difficult) (LO-17) (6 Marks)

questions.question: Analyze the poem ‘Sympathy’ by Charles Mackay focusing on the themes of kindness, gratitude and the value of human connections. How does the poet convey the importance of sympathy in human relationships?
questions.answer:
The poem "Sympathy" by Charles Mackay beautifully captures the essence of kindness, gratitude, and the value of human connections. The poet expresses deep appreciation for someone who showed sympathy and kindness, valuing it more than material wealth.

The poem highlights the theme of kindness by emphasizing the positive impact it has on individuals. The poet feels grateful and thankful for the person's sympathy, showing that kindness can bring people closer together. The line "Oh, gold is great, but greater far is heavenly sympathy" underscores the importance of sympathy over material wealth.

In conclusion, "Sympathy" is a powerful poem that celebrates the value of kindness and human connections. The poet's heartfelt appreciation for sympathy serves as a reminder of the importance of empathy and compassion in our relationships.

questions.answer: Worker bees collect nectar in their honey sacs where natural enzymes break down complex sugars. Inside the hive, they deposit the nectar into cells and fan their wings rapidly to evaporate the excess moisture until thick honey is formed.

questions.question: State any two important uses of honey in daily life.
questions.answer: Honey is widely used as a healthy natural food sweetener and energy booster. It is also used in Ayurvedic medicine to soothe sore throats, heal wounds, and aid digestion.

questions.question: Describe the responsibilities of worker bees in a hive.
questions.answer: Worker bees perform all household duties: cleaning honeycomb cells, nursing young larvae, tending to the queen, defending the entrance against intruders, and flying out to gather nectar and pollen.

sections.title: V. Paragraph Writing / Creative Expression
sections.instructions: Write a short paragraph in about 5-6 sentences. (Difficult) (LO-15) (4 Marks)

questions.question: Write a short paragraph on 'The Importance of Honeybees in Nature'.
questions.answer: Honeybees are among the most essential pollinators on Earth. While flying from blossom to blossom to gather food, they carry pollen grains that allow fruits, vegetables, flowers, and trees to reproduce. Without bees, many of the crops humans and animals depend upon for food would vanish. Furthermore, they supply humans with nutritious honey and beeswax. Protecting honeybee populations is vital for maintaining ecological balance and global food security.

questions.question: Write a short biographical sketch highlighting the courage and sacrifice of Neerja Bhanot.
questions.answer: Neerja Bhanot was born in Chandigarh on September 7, 1963. She became a model and then a senior flight purser with Pan Am. On September 5, 1986, Pan Am Flight 73 was hijacked by four armed terrorists at Karachi airport. Showing remarkable presence of mind, she alerted the pilots who escaped, preventing the hijackers from taking off. Over a harrowing 17-hour standoff, she tended to terrified passengers, hid American passports, and finally opened emergency exit chutes. As bullets flew, she shielded three innocent children and lost her life just two days before her 23rd birthday. She was posthumously honored with the Ashoka Chakra, becoming a national legend.
